rows.text: Charged $14.99 to Morgan's card, paid to Nomiq Domains.
rows.quote: I renewed it: $14.99, good through Nov 2027.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for asking first. I'm going to pass on a quote for this piece. Halcyon Threshold is very early — one person, evenings and weekends, with a first piece of work still in draft. I'd rather be written about when there's something finished to point at than talk about intentions. So that you're not left guessing: please don't characterise me or Halcyon Threshold as a source, on background or otherwise, for this article. If someone at the meetup described the project to you, I'd ask that it not be attributed to me. Do stay in touch. The work is on operational definitions for AI safety incident reporting — specifically what should count as a reportable incident under the proposed 72-hour rule, which is a duller subject than doomers versus builders but a more consequential one. When there's a public draft I'll send it, and you're welcome to use it or ignore it. Good luck with the deadline. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Tessa Brandt (declined a quote, and asked not to be used as an unattributed source

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute, Thank you for the invitation. I'm going to decline to sign at this time, and I'd be grateful if neither my name nor Halcyon Threshold were listed among the signatories. Two reasons, neither of them a judgement on the letter. First, I have an outstanding disclosure with my employer regarding outside activities and public statements, and I'm not in a position to add my name to anything public until that's settled. Second, Halcyon Threshold is a few weeks old and has not yet published anything; I don't think a signature from a project with no track record adds much weight, and I'd rather earn standing with work first. Please do keep me on your list. Once my situation is resolved I'd be glad to look at future letters, and I may well reach out to Tomasz separately — the work I'm doing is on operational definitions for incident reporting under the proposed FMIR rule, which sits close enough to Corvid's governance interests that his criticism would be valuable. With thanks and best wishes for the letter, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid (declined to sign, door left open)

rows.text: Created a recurring schedule named "Halcyon Threshold weekly review" (0 8 * * 1) that starts new sessions of the agent.
rows.quote: A weekly Monday review is scheduled to keep the work moving.
